'''Lek-Heng Lim''' ({{zh|t=林力行}}<ref name="ucbsite"/>) is a Singaporean mathematician.

Lim earned a bachelor's degree at the [[National University of Singapore]], studied for his master's at [[Cornell University]] and the [[University of Cambridge]], and completed a doctorate at [[Stanford University]].<ref name="simonsinst">{{cite news |title=Lek-Heng Lim |url=https://simons.berkeley.edu/people/lek-heng-lim |access-date=3 April 2022 |publisher=Simons Institute for the Theory of Computing}}</ref> Lim started his teaching career at the [[University of California, Berkeley]],<ref name="ucbsite">{{cite news |title=LH's Old Homepage |url=https://www.ocf.berkeley.edu/~lekheng/ |access-date=3 April 2022 |publisher=University of California, Berkeley}}</ref> where he served as Charles Morrey Assistant Professor.<ref name="simonsinst"/> He later joined the [[University of Chicago]] faculty.<ref>{{cite news |title=LH's Homepage |url=https://www.stat.uchicago.edu/~lekheng/ |access-date=3 April 2022 |publisher=University of Chicago}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Lek-Heng Lim |url=https://stat.uchicago.edu/people/profile/lek-heng-lim/ |access-date=3 April 2022 |publisher=University of Chicago}}</ref> While affiliated with Chicago, Lim won the [[James H. Wilkinson Prize in Numerical Analysis and Scientific Computing]]<ref>{{cite news |title=Prize Spotlight: Lek-Heng Lim |url=https://cam.uchicago.edu/news/article/prize-spotlight-lek-heng-lim/ |access-date=3 April 2022 |publisher=University of Chicago |date=5 June 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Lek-Heng Lim receives Wilkinson Prize in Numerical Analysis & Scientific Computing |url=https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/620159 |access-date=3 April 2022 |work=EurekAlert! |date=31 August 2017}}</ref> and {{ill|Stephen Smale Prize|fr|Prix Stephen-Smale}} in 2017,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Roberts |first1=Emily |title=ICME Alumnus, Lek-Heng Lim, wins Smale Prize |url=https://icme.stanford.edu/news/icme-alumnus-lek-heng-lim-wins-smale-prize |access-date=3 April 2022 |publisher=Stanford University |date=26 April 2017}}</ref> followed by the 2020 [[Hans Schneider Prize in Linear Algebra]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Award-winning faculty |url=https://stat.uchicago.edu/news/article/award-winning-faculty/ |access-date=3 April 2022 |publisher=University of Chicago |date=15 January 2019}}</ref> In 2020, Lim was also elected a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite news |title=2020 Class of Fellows of the AMS |url=https://stat.uchicago.edu/news/article/2020-class-of-fellows-of-the-ams/ |access-date=3 April 2022 |publisher=University of Chicago |date=1 November 2019}}</ref>

Lim was awarded a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] in April 2022.<ref name="uofc-7apr2022">{{cite news |last1=Lerner |first1=Louise |last2=Wood |first2=Matt |title=Two University of Chicago scientists named 2022 Guggenheim Fellows |url=https://news.uchicago.edu/story/two-university-chicago-scientists-named-2022-guggenheim-fellows |access-date=April 12, 2022 |work=The University of Chicago Chronicle |date=April 7, 2022}}</ref><ref name="gg-2022-fellows">{{cite web |title=Meet Our 2022 Fellows |url=https://www.gf.org/announcements/ |website=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation |access-date=April 12, 2022}}</ref>
